slides.heading: Common Characters
slides.subtitle: AlgoExpert · Easy · Strings
slides.narration: Let's solve Common Characters, an easy strings problem. We'll restate the problem, build the intuition, walk through the approach, read the Java solution, and finish with its complexity.

slides.heading: The problem
bullets: Return the unique characters that appear in every string.
slides.narration: Here's the problem. Return the unique characters that appear in every string.

slides.heading: Intuition
bullets: A character is common if it appears in every string, so count in how many strings each unique character appears.
slides.narration: A character is common if it appears in every string, so count in how many strings each unique character appears.

slides.heading: Brute force vs optimal
bullets: Brute force: for each char of word 1, scan every other word
Optimal: count distinct chars per word → O(total chars)
Use a set per word so repeats count once
slides.narration: Brute force would check each character of the first word against every other word. Counting how many words contain each distinct character does it in one pass over all the characters.

slides.heading: Approach
bullets: 1. For each string, take its set of characters
2. Count the number of strings containing each one
3. Keep characters whose count equals the number of strings
slides.narration: Step by step. First, for each string, take its set of characters. Second, count the number of strings containing each one. Third, keep characters whose count equals the number of strings.

slides.heading: Java solution
slides.narration: We loop over the strings, build a set of each string's characters, and increment counts in a map. Finally, we collect characters whose count equals the number of strings.

slides.heading: Complexity
slides.narration: Time is O of n times m. Space is O of c distinct chars.

slides.heading: Edge cases & pitfalls
bullets: Count each char once per word (use a set)
Single word → all its unique chars
slides.narration: Use a set per word so repeated letters count once. A single word returns all its unique characters.

slides.heading: Interview tips & follow-ups
bullets: Optimise: start from the shortest word's chars
slides.narration: An optimisation starts from the shortest word. A follow-up includes multiplicity, keeping minimum counts per character.

slides.heading: Recap
bullets: A character is common if it appears in every string, so count in how many strings each unique character appears.
